title: NEED GRID
body: I am not a photography expert whatsoever, but having the grid to place things on the lines has been a trick I like to use. It's the only thing about photography that I know. Without it, it's a little hard to feel like too much has been stripped out of the process. You know what I mean?

title: Great but needs fixes

Also, on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, you have 0.5, 1, and 4, but the ones in between are missing. You have to press the button to get to those levels, but for quick shooting, it really gets in the way. Every time I open the app, it asks me for location permissions, which makes fast shooting also a problem. Overall, I love the app. I'm still using it right now. I'm loving it. Just needs those fixes

title: Please change app icon
body: Please, change the app icon. I’d like to add it too my home screen but the colors and design clash hard compared to all of my other apps so I have to hide it in my App Library. At the very least have other icon options in the settings.

title: Missing x2 Camera
body: Enjoying this app and love the processing however it's missing the x2 camera option. Why?

title: Editing bug
body: When editing photos there is a bug where it shifts the frame off center.

title: I thought this did more
body: I have to assume anyone buying this would think it does significantly more than it actually does. It also doesn’t let you calibrate while looking at outputs and does middling processing that make previews prettier than results. You should probably spend your money elsewhere! No refund option and no more buying things based on Twitter convos for me

title: Fine except Forward Facing
body: I’ve overall really enjoyed this app, but I keep running into the forward facing camera being immensely washed out and bright versus the back facing camera. I believe the two need different settings, purely because to fix the forward, I have to make the back look pretty rough. There’s no winning there.

title: 28MP maximum
body: Quality is good, but export is limited to 28MP maximum, and that’s a big deal to me personally.

title: Great but needs some work!
body: Images look great but it drains my battery insanely fast and makes my phone hotter than it does when I’m using my phone to game, which seems kind of crazy for a camera app.

title: Wonderful, but has weird restrictive aspect ratio rules
body: Photos that come out of the box are wonderful and the ability to automatically apply your own fine-tuned settings is great. My only gripe is in how I prefer to shoot in 16:9 and there is a 16:9 configuration for the camera, but it forces it to always be in landscape mode, so each portrait 16:9 photo I take has to be manually rotated. It’s even more bizarre when I set a custom 9:16 aspect ratio, which actually crops the viewfinder down into a landscape orientation…when holding the phone vertically. It makes no sense to me.

title: Amazing Processing/ Color
body: Love the app and the approach to manipulating the Apple raw. The image adjustments are great but it desperately needs a “sharpen” option as the raw images from the phone eliminate all sharpening making all the images too soft. I have to drop final export into another app to add sharpening.

title: Auto Photo Save Doesn’t Work From Lock Screen
body: The app is great except for the title. While any photos taken from an unlocked phone will save to the camera roll automatically, any photos taken from a widget in the lock screen must later be manually exported to the photo library. Sounds small (and it is, hence only one star deducted) but it’s a meaningful frustration that gets in the way of using it as a default “pull out the phone and snap a quick pic of the sunset” app.

title: Really cool editing app, however…
body: Really cool editing app! However, the max shooting resolution is 4032*3024. The max resolution on lots of other camera apps (ProCam, Halide, even the vanilla camera app) is 8064*6048. Recently, ProCam came out with an update that allows full resolution capture without any of Apple’s processing. That would be a nice feature to have in this app as well! It’s still my go-to app for providing a filmic look to my photos on the go.

title: Love it!
body: Only critique is I’d love a rule of thirds option when taking the picture!

title: Good, but having a bug issue
body: Loving the app so far. However, I am having an issue. At the editing screen, when I start moving sliders the image will jump to right and be about 30% off-screen. Not a deal-breaker, but makes tweaking my images a bit of a hassle. Please fix!

title: Good app with hiccups
body: I enjoy it so far but I’m unsure about the choices on some of the settings. When I check a photo it automatically will go back to the back camera, even if I’m using the front camera, so I have to change it every single time. Another thing that could be integrated is the fact that the timer resets to 0 after every shot, meaning you have to open the timer to set it, take the photo, go back to the timer settings and add it again, take the photo, rinse and repeat. Keeping the timer set until closing the app or manually changing it back to 0 would be a nice add.

title: Great app, amazing photo processing.
body: Chromagraph camera is truly an amazing app, love how it is a one time cost rather than a subscription. The photo editing and processing is truly cinematic and beyond my expectations. You really are able to capture the emotion in each photo. Though my one critique would have to be how the direct photo shoot mode only takes 12 mp raw photos rather than the 48 mp photos my iPhone 17 pro is capable of taking , this is the only think holding me back from using this app as my primary camera app. Can’t wait for the addition of video editing! And again, great app, especially for its price.

title: Very nice, but needs sharpening features added ASAP.
body: Very nice app. Love the general features and focus. However, I was disappointed when I zoomed into 100% on my images. A RAW photo processor needs sharpening tools that the app is currently missing. RAW photos are naturally unsharpened and appear to lack detail. The details are in the RAW, but need to be unlocked by applying sharpening during output. Photographers who edit RAW images know that they need to apply sharpening before conversion to JPEG or HEIF, and even more sharpening before printing. Direct conversion to JPG or HEIF without any sharpening just looks bad, even if you layer faux grain on top. Apple’s default camera has sharpening baked in. This app doesn’t, so its output currently appears muddy and lacking detail.

title: Great replacement camera app
body: I like this app, but it seems like it doesn’t parse some types of imported RAW files correctly - my Ricoh GR3 RAWs can be imported, but Lumix S9 and Lumix L10 don’t show up. It may be that the way the iPhone imports “RAW+HEIF” or “RAW+JPEG” is breaking things. So to edit captures from other devices, there’s a stumbling block, but as an alternative to the default iPhone camera this is great.

title: great app!
body: thought $13 was a little pricey for a camera, but i love it! the photos come out so clean and looks like film. my only grief is that it doesn’t have grid lines, but overall it’s great.

title: Please improve UI flow
body: I already love this app from a technical perspective. It takes beautiful photos immediately and the editing controls are lovely. I’ve used a lot of camera apps that do away with apple’s processing and this is on track to be my favorite. Unfortunately, some of the ui elements are in kind of baffling places, especially on the Duo. For example, when looking at the photos I took in the app, I can’t swipe down too close the gallery and the tiny button to go back to the camera is at the upper left of the screen, instead of somewhere easily reachable (like in the empty sidebar). I’m really hoping to see some minor ui tweaks that address this and other ease of use issues.

title: Great work, needs some slight UI fixes

When editing the image, the view of the picture often glitches and I can’t see parts of the picture. The buttons to navigate between different screens/views are cumbersome at times and hard to use. A couple streamlining fixes from a UI/UX perspective would be very appreciated! Overall great experience with the app though!

body: Honestly I thought it was kind of hype and even though I love Yedlin and Rian I didn’t think the app could be that great. I was 1000% so wrong and I’m thrilled that was wrong. It’s the best photography app since the original Instagram. 10/10 must buy

title: Street photography with iPhone unlocked
body: Love this. Simple interface, great default highlight weighted exposure, very nice grain effect. Though lots of features—masking, adjusting halation amount, flipping to b&w in the edit not just in the camera before shooting, and locking white balance—are still missing, this is already my go to phone camera app.

title: one stop shop!
body: the best camera really is the one you always have with you, and now i feel like i have one i *want* to have with me. as a cinematographer i have been a longtime fan of Steve Yedlin’s work, and reader of his incredible technical writing on color pipelines. one of my favorite philosophies of his is that we should be “look authors and not look shoppers”, meaning that we don’t just have to accept a manufacturer’s given look. i have spent years roundtripping my iphone photos through 3 different apps in an attempt to wrestle away some of the undesirable effects of the standard issue camera app — and while i’ve only spent a few hours with chromagraph — i think i’ve finally found the level of control i’ve been looking for. the images look beautiful, and the user interface is slick and easy to navigate. i’m excited to make this a part of my process!

Also more manual controls in the future. At that point just take my money. One of the few people I still have respect for in the film industry
